name: text-autosize
title: Auto-sized title
summary: A one-line bold title that picks the largest font size between 12 and 48 that fits its card, so it is large on a wide card and small on a narrow one.
prompt: Make a card title that automatically shrinks its font to fit the card width, between 12 and 48 sp, on one line.
teaches: Let a text choose its own size with autoSize true, bounded by minFontSize and maxFontSize
Give an auto-sized text a width to fit (fillMaxWidth) and keep it on one line with maxLines 1
Check a responsive text by rendering the same document at several widths
pitfalls: minFontSize and maxFontSize alone change nothing: autoSize must be true for the player to search between them
An auto-sized text needs a bounded width; in a box that wraps its content there is nothing to fit to, so give the text fillMaxWidth (or a fixed width)
Without maxLines 1 the player may prefer wrapping onto two lines at a larger size over shrinking a single line

snippets.note: autoSize true, minFontSize 12, maxFontSize 48, maxLines 1, fillMaxWidth

check.describe: At 400×120 the title fills the card's width in large letters; rendered at 150×120 (render_rc with width/height) it should be much smaller and still whole on one line (the TS player does this; the C++ player still clips it: EXAMPLES_FINDINGS C14). The narrow render is the resize check (C++ still clips it, C14); at 600 wide the title stops growing at maxFontSize 48.
